assessment: K0002-K0005 are supported by their declared Evidence and preserve their main qualifications. K0006 correctly synthesizes the supervisory/constraint/fallback architecture at a high level, but K0001/K0006 can be read as universally assigning process safety functions to an independent SIS/SIF-type layer. The selected functional-safety evidence supports independence where hazard/risk analysis and required risk reduction make it necessary; it does not establish a universal allocation rule for every safety function.

findings.impact: The wording can overgeneralize the functional-safety evidence into a universal requirement that all process safety functions be assigned to independent SIS/SIF or equivalent protection. IEC establishes the safe-state role of SIS when used, while the HSE material makes the required separation/independence dependent on hazard/risk assessment and the safety functions/risk reduction involved. This does not overturn the layered supervisory architecture, but it affects the methodological validity of safety-function allocation in a high-stakes design context.

repair_direction.instruction: Qualify K0001/K0006 so hazard/risk analysis determines which safety functions require SIS/SIF or other independent protection and the necessary degree of BPCS/supervisory-path independence. Preserve the common-dangerous-failure/dependency principle, then rebuild 30_analysis from the repaired Synthesis.
